A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from EMN to MemFlow. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification accuracy, adaptation timing, component ablations and sensitivity results on four cross-domain benchmarks, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional SFUDA integrations, spiking-model comparisons, gradient-free comparisons and component analyses.

M1.justification: The four-stage memory architecture is retained, but Section 10.2 adds an SFUDA integration that uses MemFlow confidence to weight another model's training loss, including an added pseudo-labeling step for AaD. Equations (8) and (17) also change the documented dispersion updates from averaged absolute deviations to squared-deviation variance updates; this exceeds renaming or notation changes.

E1.justification: The four datasets and Digits/Office transfer tasks are retained. VisDA-C coverage is inconsistent in v3: Section 10.1 says R->S is no longer considered, while Section 4.1 explicitly retains both directions and Table 2 retains the earlier two-direction average. Whether that test scenario was actually removed cannot be established reliably.

E2.justification: V3 removes the evaluated CDAN comparison and adds AaD and PFC alongside retained SHOT and TPDS. Supplementary Table 6 and Figure 9 newly evaluate LIF, SRM, ALIF, ELM, ESN and Hopfield comparators. The classical DAMap classifiers largely remain under retrain@ names; their renaming is not an added baseline.

E3.justification: V3 Section 10.1 introduces mean per-class accuracy for VisDA-C S->R, differing from v2's reported per-task accuracy and two-direction average. New experiments introduce SFUDA integration, spiking substitutions, independent hub/bridge grids and propagation/update-rate sweeps. The existing backbone choices, batch size of 64 and 16-epoch best-result selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 ablates Gaussian blur and confidence updating and varies hub/bridge counts together. V3 adds confidence-only and spiking-removal configurations, substitutes alternative spiking mechanisms, varies hub and bridge counts independently on two datasets, and analyzes propagation steps and update rate. Its supplementary epoch trajectories also retain fewer representative tasks.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, experimental confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Memory confidence and Gaussian variance describe the model, not uncertainty in reported experimental results.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial SFUDA integration, spiking, gradient-free and ablation results. For example, v2 Table 5 reports Office-Home SHOT at 71.8%, whereas v3 Table 1 reports 71.0% and adds SHOT+MemFlow at 72.3%. Existing DAMap accuracies mostly persist after rounding. V3's supplementary VisDA-C 60.4% uses a different metric and cannot establish a decline from v2's 72.08% two-direction average.

T1.justification: V2 treats Gaussian memory distributions as an assumption and supplies no convergence proof. V3 introduces Gaussian-distribution and reinforced-memorization convergence theorems, associated assumptions and lemmas, and extensive supplementary proofs. Section 9 also adds a derivation of the fuzzy-memory convolution formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: gradient-free distributed memorization, spiking accumulation, Gaussian fuzzy memory and reinforced adaptation with a frozen backbone. The headline claims of up to 10% improvement and less than 1% adaptation time also remain; the new name does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 broadens the mechanism and applicability discussion beyond v2's overfitting and confidence-update explanations. It adds neuron-balancing and persistent-memory interpretations, attributes excessive propagation to information loss, discusses update-rate underfitting/overfitting, and explains MemFlow's SFUDA instructor role. It also qualifies integration efficiency by identifying additional pseudo-labeling overhead for AaD.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository link and documents SFUDA loss weighting and update scheduling. Conversely, several explicit baseline details from v2, including MLP hidden width, SVM gamma and BLS incremental steps, are omitted or compressed into default-configuration descriptions. The PDFs do not establish whether the linked code is accessible.

R1.justification: The related-work positioning shifts from a broad UDA discussion to an explicit UDA/SFUDA distinction, with stronger comparisons to last-layer retraining and spiking networks. V3 adds SFUDA surveys, AaD/PFC, last-layer and Hopfield-related references while removing several earlier alignment discussions and the Liquid State Machine reference.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming EMN to MemFlow, v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and related work, reorganizes experimental reporting into dedicated subsections, and restructures the supplement around proofs, derivations and expanded experiments. This is substantial narrative revision rather than isolated editing.

P2.justification: V3 adds an introductory comparison diagram, consolidates accuracy and timing into redesigned tables, replaces the network-size line plot with two-dimensional heatmaps, and adds parameter and comparator displays. Numerous per-task plots are condensed or removed. The framework and memory visualizations are retained with changed placement and sizing.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support through broader comparisons, component analyses and SFUDA integration. However, its new theoretical guarantees introduce reliability problems: Section 8 incorrectly infers almost-sure convergence from the positive probability bound in Eq. (41). Runtime reporting also conflicts, including Office31 MemFlow time of 0.160 ms in Table 2 versus 0.016 ms in Figure 6. These substantive benefits and new inconsistencies prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
